greek: Μετὰ δὲ τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα ἐγενήθη ῥῆμα κυρίου πρὸς Αβραμ ἐν ὁράματι λέγων Μὴ φοβοῦ, Αβραμ· ἐγὼ ὑπερασπίζω σου· ὁ μισθός σου πολὺς ἔσται σφόδρα.
hint: In a vision the word of the Lord tells Abram not to fear: the Lord shields him, and his wage will be very great.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾānōkî māgēn lāk*, *I am a shield to you*, a noun. The Greek has a verb, ὑπερασπίζω, *I cover with a shield*, from LSJ.
ῥῆμα is first *that which is said or spoken*, then *a word, saying*.
The aorist passive form of γίνομαι, read as the middle ἐγένετο is: `came into being`.
The present imperative of φοβέομαι, in the chain of GEN 3:10: `be put to flight`.
Glossed again, first in this chapter.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after|μετά + accusative]] [[the things which are said|the things which are said and spoken, the words, the sayings, the phrases, the subjects of speech and things, the verbs|ῥῆμα]] [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[came into being|came to be, arose, was brought into existence|γίνομαι]] [[that which is said|that which is said and spoken, a word, a saying, a phrase, the subject of speech and a thing, a verb|ῥῆμα]] [[of lord|of lord, of master, of the one having power and authority over|κύριος]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[name:Αβραμ]] [[in that which is seen|within, inside of, and by means of that which is seen, a sight and spectacle|ἐν; ὅραμα]] [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling|λέγω]] [[not|not, that not, perhaps, surely not and you don't mean to say that|μή]] [[be put to flight|be put to flight, flee affrighted, flee, be seized with fear, be affrighted, fear|φοβέομαι]], [[name:Αβραμ]]; I [[I cover with a shield|I cover with a shield, I defend|ὑπερασπίζω]] of you; [[the wages|the wages, the pay and hire, the recompense and reward, the payment and requital|μισθός]] of you [[many|many, often, much and mighty and great, deep, loud, strong, large and wide, far, long|πολύς]] will be [[very|very, very much, exceedingly, violently, far, most certainly|σφόδρα]].

names.gloss: (Αβραμ, from Hebrew ʾAbrām, "the father is exalted")

greek: λέγει δὲ Αβραμ Δέσποτα, τί μοι δώσεις; ἐγὼ δὲ ἀπολύομαι ἄτεκνος· ὁ δὲ υἱὸς Μασεκ τῆς οἰκογενοῦς μου, οὗτος Δαμασκὸς Ελιεζερ.
hint: Abram asks the Master what he will give, since he departs childless; the son of Masek, his homeborn maid, is Eliezer of Damascus.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾĂdōnāy YHWH*. The Greek has δεσπότης alone; at 15:8 it has Δέσποτα κύριε.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *hôlēk ʿărîrî*, *I go childless*. The Greek has ἀπολύομαι, *I am loosed from*, *released*.

notes.lemma: ὁ δὲ υἱὸς Μασεκ τῆς οἰκογενοῦς μου, οὗτος Δαμασκὸς Ελιεζερ
notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ûben-mešeq bêtî hûʾ Dammeśeq ʾĔlîʿezer*, *and the son of the possession of my house is Damascus Eliezer*; *mešeq* occurs nowhere else. The Greek makes it a woman's name, Μασεκ, *my home-born* slave.
Δαμασκός names the man with Eliezer here, and takes his gender; it is glossed as the city's name, which it is.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

names.gloss: (Μασεκ, from Hebrew mešeq, which the Hebrew does not use as a name, of uncertain meaning)
(Δαμασκός, from Hebrew Dammeśeq, of uncertain meaning)
(Ελιεζερ, from Hebrew ʾĔlîʿezer, "my God is help")

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Αβραμ Ἐπειδὴ ἐμοὶ οὐκ ἔδωκας σπέρμα, ὁ δὲ οἰκογενής μου κληρονομήσει με.
hint: Abram says God has given him no seed, so one born in his house will inherit from him.

notes.text: Middle Liddell has no ἐπειδή, and LSJ sends it to ἐπεί, *after that, since*, whose chain it takes.
κληρονομέω is first *to receive a share of an inheritance*, then *to inherit*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: καὶ εὐθὺς φωνὴ κυρίου ἐγένετο πρὸς αὐτὸν λέγων Οὐ κληρονομήσει σε οὗτος, ἀλλʼ ὃς ἐξελεύσεται ἐκ σοῦ, οὗτος κληρονομήσει σε.
hint: The voice of the Lord answers that not this one, but one coming out of Abram himself, will inherit from him.

notes.text: Middle Liddell's second entry, the adverb: εὐθύ *straight* of place, εὐθύς *straightway, forthwith, at once* of time, which heads it.
ἀλλά is first *otherwise, but*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: ἐξήγαγεν δὲ αὐτὸν ἔξω καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἀνάβλεψον δὴ εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἀρίθμησον τοὺς ἀστέρας, εἰ δυνήσῃ ἐξαριθμῆσαι αὐτούς. καὶ εἶπεν Οὕτως ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα σου.
hint: The Lord brings Abram outside to look up and count the stars: so will his seed be.

notes.text: Paul quotes the words at Romans 4:18: κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον· Οὕτως ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα σου.
Perseus tags δή's opening only as *exactness*, a description, and its other tags are pieces of examples; the entry's own gloss, *now, in truth, indeed, surely, really*, is the chain.
ἀστήρ is *a star*, and *a flame, light, fire*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take them for a proper name.

greek: καὶ ἐπίστευσεν Αβραμ τῷ θεῷ, καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην.
hint: Abram believes God, and it is counted to him for righteousness: Paul's text, passive where the Hebrew is active.

notes.lemma: ἐπίστευσεν Αβραμ τῷ θεῷ, καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην
notes.text: Quoted at Romans 4:3 and James 2:23, Ἐπίστευσεν δὲ Ἀβραὰμ τῷ θεῷ, καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην; at Galatians 3:6, καθὼς Ἀβραὰμ ἐπίστευσεν τῷ θεῷ; and its last clause at Romans 4:22.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *wĕheʾĕmin baYHWH wayyaḥšĕbehā lô ṣĕdāqâ*, *he believed in YHWH, and he counted it to him as righteousness*. The Greek has *the God*, and the passive, *it was counted*.
πιστεύω is first *to trust, trust to or in, put faith in, rely on, believe in*.
The aorist passive of λογίζομαι, *to count, reckon, calculate*, in the passive; *to form calculations*, which has no passive, is left out.

greek: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτόν Ἐγὼ ὁ θεὸς ὁ ἐξαγαγών σε ἐκ χώρας Χαλδαίων ὥστε δοῦναί σοι τὴν γῆν ταύτην κληρονομῆσαι.
hint: God names himself as the one who brought Abram out of the land of the Chaldeans, to give him this land to inherit.

[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads αὐτῷ.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

hint: Abram cuts them in two and lays each half facing the other; the birds he does not divide.

hint: Birds come down on the carcasses, and Abram sits down with them.

greek: καὶ ἐρρέθη πρὸς Αβραμ Γινώσκων γνώσῃ ὅτι πάροικον ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα σου ἐν γῇ οὐκ ἰδίᾳ, καὶ δουλώσουσιν αὐτοὺς καὶ κακώσουσιν αὐτοὺς καὶ ταπεινώσουσιν αὐτοὺς τετρακόσια ἔτη.
hint: Abram is told his seed will sojourn in a land not their own, enslaved, ill-treated and humbled four hundred years.

notes.text: Stephen gives the words at Acts 7:6: ὅτι ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα αὐτοῦ πάροικον ἐν γῇ ἀλλοτρίᾳ, καὶ δουλώσουσιν αὐτὸ καὶ κακώσουσιν ἔτη τετρακόσια.
A participle with the finite verb of the same word, as the Hebrew *yādōaʿ tēdaʿ* doubles it.

greek: τὸ δὲ ἔθνος, ᾧ ἐὰν δουλεύσωσιν, κρινῶ ἐγώ· μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα ἐξελεύσονται ὧδε μετὰ ἀποσκευῆς πολλῆς.
hint: God will judge the nation they serve; afterwards they will come out with many goods.

notes.lemma: τὸ δὲ ἔθνος, ᾧ ἐὰν δουλεύσωσιν, κρινῶ ἐγώ
notes.text: Acts 7:7 continues: καὶ τὸ ἔθνος ᾧ ἐὰν δουλεύσουσιν κρινῶ ἐγώ.
κρίνω is first *to pick out, choose*; *to judge* is its fourth.
ὧδε is first *in this wise, so, thus*; *hither, here* comes last.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the number of people accustomed to live together|the number of people accustomed to live together, the company and body of men, the host, the swarms and flocks, the nation and people, the nations and gentiles, the special class, the caste and tribe, the sex|ἔθνος]], to which ever [[they may be slaves|they may be slaves, they may serve and be subject to|δουλεύω]], [[I will separate|I will separate and part and put asunder and distinguish, I will pick out and choose, I will pick out for oneself and choose, I will decide, I will judge, I will adjudge, I will judge of and estimate, I will expound and interpret, I will determine, I will question, I will bring to trial and accuse, I will pass sentence upon and condemn, I will be chosen, I will be brought to trial|κρίνω]] I; [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after|μετά + accusative]] [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[they will go out of|they will go out of, they will come out, they will go away and march off, they will go forth|ἐξέρχομαι]] [[in this wise|in this wise and so and thus, so very and so exceedingly, thus and as follows, hither and here|ὧδε]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] [[of removal|of removal and riddance, of baggage, of household stuff, of ordure and filth|ἀποσκευή]] [[of much|of much and mighty and great, of many, of deep, of loud, of strong, of large and wide, of far, of long, often|πολύς]].

greek: σὺ δὲ ἀπελεύσῃ πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας σου μετʼ εἰρήνης, ταφεὶς ἐν γήρει καλῷ.
hint: Abram himself will go to his fathers in peace, buried in a good old age.

notes.text: The aorist passive of θάπτω, *to pay the last dues to a corpse, to honour with funeral rites*, in the passive.
γῆρας, *old age*, one sense, plain text.
[[flag]] ταφείς is Grabe's correction; Codex Alexandrinus reads τραφείς, *having been reared*.

reading: you [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[you will go away|you will go away, you will depart from, you will depart, you will depart from life|ἀπέρχομαι]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[the fathers|the fathers, the grandfathers|πατήρ]] of you [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] [[of peace|of peace, of time of peace|εἰρήνη]], [[having had the last dues paid|having had the last dues paid to a corpse, having been honoured with funeral rites, having been buried and interred|θάπτω]] [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to old age [[to beautiful|to beautiful, to beauteous, to fair, to good|καλός]].

greek: τετάρτη δὲ γενεὰ ἀποστραφήσονται ὧδε· οὔπω γὰρ ἀναπεπλήρωνται αἱ ἁμαρτίαι τῶν Αμορραίων ἕως τοῦ νῦν.
hint: The fourth generation will return, for the Amorites' sins are not yet full.

notes.text: Rahlfs prints the nominative, *the fourth generation*, with a plural verb after it.
The perfect passive of ἀναπληρόω, *to fill up*, the chain of GEN 2:21, with the perfect's standing state.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[fourth|fourth, a fourth time, fourthly, a fourth day|τέταρτος]] [[race|race, stock and family, breed, tribe and nation, generation, offspring, birth-place, age and time of life|γενεά]] [[they will be turned|they will be turned, they will be turned back, they will be turned away, they will be brought back, they will turn oneself about|ἀποστρέφω]] [[in this wise|in this wise and so and thus, so very and so exceedingly, thus and as follows, hither and here|ὧδε]]; [[for|for, since and as, for otherwise and else, now, but, why and what, would that|γάρ]] [[not yet|not yet, no longer and no more, not and not at all|οὔπω]] [[have been filled up|have been filled up and stand filled up, have been made up and supplied and stand so, have been filled and stand filled, have been paid in full and stand so|ἀναπληρόω]] [[the failures|the failures, the faults and sins, the guilts and sins|ἁμαρτία]] of the [[name:Αμορραίων]] [[until|until, till, while, so long as|ἕως]] of the thing [[now at this very time|now at this very time, now, of the present, the present time, just now and but now, as it is and as the case now stands, in this case|νῦν]].

names.gloss: (Αμορραῖος, from Hebrew ʾĔmōrî, of uncertain meaning)

greek: ἐπεὶ δὲ ἐγίνετο ὁ ἥλιος πρὸς δυσμαῖς, φλὸξ ἐγένετο, καὶ ἰδοὺ κλίβανος καπνιζόμενος καὶ λαμπάδες πυρός, αἳ διῆλθον ἀνὰ μέσον τῶν διχοτομημάτων τούτων.
hint: At sunset a smoking furnace and torches of fire pass between the pieces.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *waʿălāṭâ hāyâ*, *and there was thick darkness*. The Greek has *a flame came into being*.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *wĕlappîd ʾēš*, *a torch of fire*, singular. The Greek has the plural.
Middle Liddell files κλίβανος under the Attic κρίβανος, *an earthen vessel, a pan*.

καπνίζω's first sense, *to make smoke, i. e. to make a fire*, takes no object that a passive could make its subject; its second, *to smoke, blacken with smoke*, heads the passive participle, and the first follows.

reading: [[after that|after that, after, since, when, from the time when and ever since, whenever, as soon as, seeing that, for, although, else and otherwise|ἐπεί]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[was coming into being|was coming to be, was arising, was being brought into existence|γίνομαι]] [[the sun|the sun, the day and a day, Helios the sun-god|ἥλιος]] [[hard by|hard by, near, at, on, in, among, close to, before and in the presence of, upon and against, employed in, in addition to and besides|πρός + dative]] [[to settings|to settings, to quarters of sunset and wests|δυσμή]], [[a flame|a flame, a flash, the fiery strength|φλόξ]] [[came into being|came to be, arose, was brought into existence|γίνομαι]], and [[lo|lo, behold, see there|ἰδού]] [[an earthen vessel|an earthen vessel, a pan|κλίβανος]] [[being smoked|being smoked and blackened with smoke, making smoke and making a fire, being black with smoke|καπνίζω]] and [[torches|torches, beacon-lights, oil-lamps, lights, torch-races, races|λαμπάς]] [[of fire|of fire, of the funeral-fire, of the fire of the hearth|πῦρ]], which [[went through|went through, passed through, went through in detail|διέρχομαι]] [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two|ἀνά + accusative; μέσος]] [[of the halves of a thing cut in two|of the halves of a thing cut in two, of the portions of a thing cut up|διχοτόμημα]] [[of these|of these, of the nearer, of what follows|οὗτος]].

greek: ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ διέθετο κύριος τῷ Αβραμ διαθήκην λέγων Τῷ σπέρματί σου δώσω τὴν γῆν ταύτην ἀπὸ τοῦ ποταμοῦ Αἰγύπτου ἕως τοῦ ποταμοῦ τοῦ μεγάλου, ποταμοῦ Εὐφράτου,
hint: That day the Lord covenants with Abram to give his seed this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river Euphrates.

notes.text: διατίθεμαι, the middle, and διαθήκη, the chains of GEN 9:17 and 6:18.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: τοὺς Καιναίους καὶ τοὺς Κενεζαίους καὶ τοὺς Κεδμωναίους
hint: The peoples whose land is given: the Kenites, the Kenizzites and the Kadmonites.

notes.text: The peoples stand in the accusative after τὴν γῆν ταύτην, with no verb of their own.

reading: the [[name:Καιναίους]] and the [[name:Κενεζαίους]] and the [[name:Κεδμωναίους]]

(Κενεζαῖος, from Hebrew Qĕnizzî, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ τοὺς Χετταίους καὶ τοὺς Φερεζαίους καὶ τοὺς Ραφαϊν
hint: More of the peoples: the Hittites, the Perizzites and the Rephaim.

notes.text: The Hebrew plural, transliterated, as τοὺς Λουδιιμ at 10:13.

reading: and the [[name:Χετταίους]] and the [[name:Φερεζαίους]] and the [[name:Ραφαϊν]]

greek: καὶ τοὺς Αμορραίους καὶ τοὺς Χαναναίους καὶ τοὺς Ευαίους καὶ τοὺς Γεργεσαίους καὶ τοὺς Ιεβουσαίους.
hint: The last of the peoples: the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Hivites, the Girgashites and the Jebusites.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew list has ten peoples and no Hivites. The Greek adds τοὺς Ευαίους.

reading: and the [[name:Αμορραίους]] and the [[name:Χαναναίους]] and the [[name:Ευαίους]] and the [[name:Γεργεσαίους]] and the [[name:Ιεβουσαίους]].
